situation (example wording): Every decline, question back, button and note the user reads: "I can't apply 'victim': clearance figures count offense records, not other units."
what the app does today: Engine wording reached users: "Not in the slice yet", policy ids, "I can't apply", "I couldn't interpret", code names.
proposed behavior: Every user-facing string says in plain words what the data records, says why the question can't be answered as asked, and offers the nearest answerable question as a button whenever one exists (the full question is shown on the button, and it runs only when chosen). It never uses engine vocabulary: units, records as a noun, slice, shadow, policy ids, "apply", "interpret", dimension or field names, code names, "reading", "plan", "v0". Example: "Clearances are recorded for each offense, not for each person, so they can't be counted by 'victim'." A test fails if any engine word reaches user-facing text.
exact default or choices offered: Plain words; why it can't be answered; the nearest answerable question as a button.
why: Jeff, on the engine's text in the preview: "The answers need to be much, much more crystal clear for users."
test cases: Tests that cite this row: scripts/test-nibrs-shadow.ts, scripts/test-nibrs-plain-wording.ts.
